blocks.text: Organic chemistry is organised around functional groups. Although millions of organic compounds are known, there are only a handful of functional groups, and each one defines a family of compounds. A functional group is the part of an organic compound where most of its reactions take place.

In organic synthesis chemists design possible ways of building a target molecule from simpler, easily available components. Functional groups play a central role: they let chemists predict and control the reactions that lead to the desired product. Identifying the functional groups in a compound also helps to predict its properties, which matters for developing new products and for ensuring the purity and composition of products such as medicines and food additives.
